thread.title: Tech Today: Broadcom Walking Away? Amazon V Google, Praising PayPal, Synaptics

author: Tiernan Ray
title: Tech Today: Broadcom Walking Away? Amazon V Google, Praising PayPal, Synaptics
text:
Here are some things going on today in your world of tech:
Broadcom walking away?
Qualcomm ( QCOM ) shares sagged in early trading by 2%, after Broadcom ( AVGO ), as expected raised its offer for the company to $82, consisting of $60 in cash and $22 worth of Broadcom stock. The two have been locked in a hostile bidding war since shortly after Broadcom made its first overture in early November.
CNBC ’s David Faber a short while ago related on air that the break-up fee may be as high as $10 billion , which was not formally disclosed, without citing sources. Faber said that the offer may be Broadcom’s way to say that it made an effort, and then simply walk away from the pursuit of Qualcomm.
Qualcomm stock is now up 33 cents, half a percent, at $66.40 at the outset of regular trading.
Appraising Amazon
If it’s Monday, which it is, it must be time for another Amazon ( AMZN ) price target increase . Instinet’s Simeon Siegel raised his target to $1,700 from $1,360, citing the Q4 report last Thursday, which was “powerful,” and was a good omen for the company’s profit margins . The report “puts Amazon on a march to increasing and under appreciated profitability,” he writes.
Amazon shares are down $35.66, or 2.5%, at $1,394.29.
PayPal, GrubHub, Sprint
Shares of PayPal ( PYPL ) are down $1.20, or 1.6%, at $75.37, after Wells Fargo ’s Timothy Willi raised his rating on the shares to Outperform from Market Perform, and raised his price target to $95 from $80, writing that the opportunity in the payments “ecosystem” outweighs eBay ’s ( EBAY ) plan to lessen its dependence on PayPal, announced last week. He also likes the valuation, at 34% times 2018 estimates, relative to Visa ( V ) and MasterCard ( MA ) at 28 times.
Shares of GrubHub ( GRUB ) are down $3.60, or 5%,at. $67.05, in advance of the company’s earnings report this Thursday, February 8th , before market open, as the stock gets a downgrade from Raymond James ’s Aaron Kessler , to Market Perform from Outperform, citing the hypothesis the company is losing share in the U.S. from UberEats , the effort of the privately held ride-sharing giant, as well as what he believes are estimates for Ebitda that are “somewhat aggressive” for this year. The valuation of 27 times forward Ebitda estimates seems “less favorable,” he writes.
Shares of Sprint ( S ) are up 3 cents at $5.39, after KeyBanc Capital Markets ’s Brandon Nispel raised his rating on the shares to Sector Weight from Underweight, with a $5 “fair value” estimate, writing that “while still on somewhat shaky ground, an additional wave of cost saving initiatives and Sprint's spectrum position for 5G could be catalysts.” The big relief is that rising churn is now in “set” as an expectation, while the valuation he deems “more reasonable compared to the premium it once had."
What to do with Skyworks?
The Street is still picking through Apple ’s ( AAPL ) fiscal Q1 report on Thursday, which included lower-than-expected iPhone sales, and a forecast for revenue this quarter that implied lower sales as well.
Morgan Stanley ’s Joseph Moore and Craig Hettenbach this morning write that they have a “cautious” view about the immediate future for RF chip makers Skyworks Solutions ( SWKS ). The firm has an Underweight rating on Skyworks.
Skyworks shares are down $1.19, or 1.2%, at $97.77.
Synaptics’s bright spot
Speaking of Apple, KeyBanc’s John Vinh reiterates an Overweight rating on shares of touch-sensor controller maker Synaptics (SYNA). Synaptics’s could benefit with its “ chip-on-film ,” or CoF, technology, for LCD displays given there may be a renewed focus by Apple, and by competitors, to lower a phone’s bill of materials. The OLED display is the single biggest cost increase for the iPhone, he notes. “If Apple were to shift to 2 LCD SKUs versus 1 OLED SKU,” he writes, “in the iPhone 11, we would view this as incrementally positive for Synaptics."
Synaptics stock is down 94 cents, or 2%, at $40.26,
Get ready for Snap
Analysts are looking ahead of Snap ’s ( SNAP ) earnings on Tuesday afternoon, after the closing bell. And the outlook from several shops is pretty negative going into the report.
SunTrust Robinson Humphrey ’s Youssef Squali reiterates a Sell rating, writing that the “industry feedback on advertisers' demand for Snap inventory remained lukewarm during the quarter.” Stifel Nicolaus ’s John Egbert reiterates a Hold rating and writes that Street estimates for this year and next year, for revenue, “are unrealistically high."
And Doug Anmuth with J.P. Morgan reiterates an Underweight rating, writing that "the transition to programmatic will continue to be a headwind to Y/Y pricing in 4Q17 & we are not hearing a pick-up in advertiser demand in our industry discussions."
Snap stock today is down 28 cents, or 2%, at $13.43.
Amazon V. Google
It’s time to think seriously about Amazon’s threat to Alphabet ( GOOGL ), write Michael Nathanson and Greg Melich of the boutique Moffett Nathanson research firm. They issued a think piece exploring Amazon’s nascent advertising business, and conclude that if Amazon ends up getting 75% of its ad revenue “from dollars that would have been sent to Google,” it could amount to $10.78 per Google share in 2022, which would be 16% of Alphabet’s potential earnings. “And if that happens, it will be a problem,” they write.
Alphabet stock is down $21.42, or 2% at $1,097.78..
Speaking of Alphabet, Brian Nowak of Morgan Stanley this morning makes the case that the company should offer greater disclosure about the individual lines of business, including its cloud computing operation.
Noting that “As seen with other tech companies (Amazon and Microsoft ( MSFT )), clear recurring disclosure can enable investors to better understand and value underlying business drivers,” Nowak writes that Alphabet could show how the sum of its parts can add up to $1 trillion in market value, or $1,400 per share, by his estimates.
Nowak values the cloud business, alone, at $45 billion.
